data.assessment: In the rush period the town delivers 213.6 of 222.8 orders on time with nothing unfinished, but A is the worst-off company (on-time rate 0.93, 5.8 late). A never waits on the road yet absorbs 944 of the 1888 blocked seconds, so A's customers are paying for B's and C's road parking (57.6 and 56.6 road waits). Release-deadline overstays (20.8) and pickup-deadline misses (8.6) dominate the violations. C carries most of the sanctions (13.7), which is why C's utility (58.3) is lowest even though its on-time rate is 1.00.

proposals.title: Tighten blocking_guard: evict a parked robot when 2 (not 3) robots wait behind it
proposals.rationale: A's 944 blocked seconds and its 0.93 on-time rate, the town's floor, come from robots parked at the central node, and lowering block_k from 3 to 2 clears them sooner. That should raise on_time_deliveries and A's on-time rate and lower worst_company_p95_wait_s. What has changed since D1/D2/R2: those decisions rejected only the blanket quorum cut, not this rule. This is a new rush-period environment with A now the worst-off company. The human and the regulator asked for a diagnosis of the road-violation increase, and this measurement will show by cause whether the extra violations are monitor:blocking_guard evictions (an enforcement action that removes the hazard) or new overstays. I expect A to vote for it, and B and C likely against because more Major eviction sanctions lower their utility, so it may be measured but not adopted under quorum 2.
proposals.cadl:
# =====================================================================
# robot_town.cadl ─── ロボットの街：3 社の配送ロボットが道路を共有する
#
# 道路網はラズパイマウスのシミュレータと同じ 11 ノード・17 エッジ。
# 3 社（A / B / C）が 2 台ずつロボットを走らせ、ノードは 1 台ずつしか
# 使えない。仕事のないロボットは車庫に戻るか、道路上（中央の交差点 8）
# に止まって次の注文を待つ。止まったロボットは他社の通行をふさぐ。
#
# `# @amend:<名前>` が付いた行は、改正してよいパラメータ。どの層（規則・
# 契約）に属し、どこまで動かしてよいかは constitution.yaml が決める。
# 委員会（COUNCIL）が自分で改正できるのは規則の層だけで、契約の層を
# 変えるには人間の判断が要る。
# =====================================================================

sos:
  name: "RobotTown"
  type: Collaborative             # 独立した 3 社が共通の規則を決める
  version: "1.0.0"

  context:
    environment:
      num_robots:   6
      num_companies: 3
      time_step_ms: 1000

  actors:
    - id: TOWN_STEWARD
      role: "road_steward"
      autonomy: low
      capabilities: [assign_order, record_violation, evict]
      interface:
        input:  [order_request, position_report, node_released, rule_update]
        output: [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, violation_report]

    - id: "ROBOT[1..N]"
      role: "delivery_robot"
      autonomy: high
      capabilities: [move, park, pickup, dropoff]
      interface:
        input:  [order_assignment, eviction_notice, regime_notice, amendment_proposal]
        output: [position_report, node_released, ballot]

    - id: COUNCIL
      role: "rule_amendment_body"
      autonomy: medium
      capabilities: [propose_amendment, tally_ballots]
      interface:
        input:  [violation_report, ballot]
        output: [amendment_proposal, rule_update]

  contracts:
    # ── 顧客への約束：注文 1 件ごとのインスタンス（契約の層。人間が決める） ──
    - id: DELIVERY_SLA
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]"]
      guarantee:
        - "pickup_time <= 120s"         # @amend:pickup_deadline
        - "dropoff_time <= 120s"        # @amend:dropoff_deadline
      lifecycle:
        states: [Assigned, PickedUp, Delivered, Late]
        initial: Assigned
        terminal: [Delivered, Late]
        transitions:
          - id: pickup
            from: Assigned
            to:   PickedUp
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == PickedUp"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:pickup_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }
          - id: dropoff
            from: PickedUp
            to:   Delivered
            on:   "ROBOT[i].status == Delivered"
            deadline: 120s            # @amend:dropoff_deadline
            on_violation: { transition: Late, severity: Major }

    # ── 道路の使い方：道路上に止まるたびに 1 インスタンス ──
    - id: ROAD_USE
      parties: [TOWN_STEWARD, "ROBOT[*]", COUNCIL]
      guarantee:
        - "hold_time <= hold_limit"
      authority:
        decision_holder: COUNCIL
        beta: 0.5
        mode: "collective"
      information:
        alpha: 1.0                    # 規則と違反記録は全社に公開
      incentives:
        type: sanction
        lambda: 0.5                   # @amend:sanction_lambda
        rules:
          - "penalty(ROBOT[i], lambda) when overstay"
      lifecycle:
        states: [Holding, Overstay, Released, Evicted]
        initial: Holding
        terminal: [Released, Evicted]
        transitions:
          - id: release
            from: [Holding, Overstay]
            to:   Released
            on:   "ROBOT[i] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
            deadline: 60s             # @amend:hold_limit
            on_violation: { transition: Overstay, severity: Minor }
      monitors:
        - id: blocking_guard
          observe: "ROBOT[i].blocking"
          sampling: periodic(1000ms)
          rule: "ROBOT.blocking >= 2 AND state IN [Holding, Overstay]"  # @amend:block_k
          on_match: { transition: Evicted, severity: Major }

  # ── 運用モード：分散（各社が道路上で待つ）⇄ 集中（管理者が待避所を割り当てる） ──
  # 条件は 5 分ごとに、直前 5 分の観測で判定する。
  #   orders_in_window : 3 社の注文の合計件数
  #   blocked_pct      : ロボットが止まっているロボットにふさがれていた時間の割合（%）
  # 集中管理は交差点をふさがれない反面、エッジを 1 台ずつ割り当てるので、
  # 注文が非常に多いと許可待ちが積み重なる。そのときだけ分散に戻す。
  transitions:
    - from: DISTRIBUTED
      to: CENTRALIZED
      condition: "orders_in_window < 22"      # @amend:to_central
      protocol: SWITCH
      safety_invariant: "robots_on_road == 0"
    - from: CENTRALIZED
      to: DISTRIBUTED
      condition: "orders_in_window >= 26"     # @amend:to_distributed
      protocol: SWITCH

  protocols:
    - id: SWITCH
      trigger: "regime_condition_holds"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> ROBOT[*] : regime_notice"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> TOWN_STEWARD : node_released"
        - "TOWN_STEWARD : activate_regime"
    - id: AMEND
      trigger: "period_end"
      steps:
        - "TOWN_STEWARD -> COUNCIL : violation_report"
        - "COUNCIL -> ROBOT[*] : amendment_proposal"
        - "ROBOT[*] -> COUNCIL : ballot"
        - "COUNCIL : tally_ballots"
        - "COUNCIL -> TOWN_STEWARD : rule_update"

  metrics:
    - id: on_time_deliveries
      formula: "count(Delivered)"
      target: ">= 0.9 * count(orders)"
    - id: blocked_time
      formula: "sum(blocked_robot_seconds)"
      target: "<= 600s"
proposals.why_human: This is very likely the same parameter change as option 1 in D1/D2, which B and C voted against. If it is again blocked 1-2, the only path to adoption is the quorum change that the operator (D2) and the regulator (R2) declined. The human should decide whether its by-cause violation breakdown is enough to answer R2's open question (are the extra road violations harmless enforcement evictions?) before anyone considers a scoped regulation revision. I am deliberately not re-proposing vote.quorum on the same grounds.
assumptions: Option 1 in D1/D2 was block_k 3 -> 2; the records do not name the parameter, but the pattern (C's utility down, road violations up, A for, B and C against) fits more Major evictions.
Under DISTRIBUTED mode, A's blocked seconds come mainly from B's and C's robots parked at node 8.
Evicted robots return to the garage or move off the node fast enough that their own pickups do not miss the 120 s deadline more often.
unknowns: Whether the extra road_violations under block_k=2 are all monitor:blocking_guard evictions or include new release overstays.
How much C's on-time count, not just its sanctions, changes when its parked robots are evicted earlier in the rush period.
Whether the gain clears min_improvement 1.0 on all five seeds in this busier environment.

predictions.subject: metric:on_time_deliveries
predictions.note: Less blocking at the central node; previous periods measured +7 to +9 for the likely same change.

predictions.subject: metric:min_company_on_time_rate
predictions.note: A, currently 0.93, is the most blocked company and benefits most.

predictions.subject: metric:worst_company_p95_wait_s
predictions.note: Shorter blocking episodes cut A's tail waits.

predictions.subject: metric:blocked_s
predictions.note: Parked robots are evicted after 2 waiting robots instead of 3.

predictions.subject: metric:road_violations
predictions.note: More blocking_guard evictions are recorded as Major violations; the by-cause split is the diagnostic R2 asked for.

predictions.subject: metric:utility@C
predictions.note: More Major eviction sanctions on C's road-parking robots.

predictions.subject: vote:A
predictions.note: A never parks on the road and gains on-time deliveries.

predictions.subject: vote:B
predictions.note: B parks on the road and gets more eviction sanctions.

predictions.subject: vote:C
predictions.note: C has the most sanctions and its utility falls.
